automation_name: AI Dev Wiki Leaf Update Watch

cutoff_window.policy: Only public sources published or visibly updated within the last 7 days relative to run time qualify.

qualifying_updates.visible_date_evidence: Qwen Code weekly page shows 2026-09-17 and describes three stable releases shipped that week.
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Qwen Code added built-in handoff to Claude Code and Codex subagents, named workflow execution, message-level token caps, run structure previews, subagent thinking depth/tool restrictions, permission rebinding to exact workflow versions, goal turn/time caps, context accounting, and cross-session messaging.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Local workflow pages should watch whether terminal-agent orchestration practice is moving toward explicit subagent launch contracts, foreground permission visibility, bounded goals, and pre-run dispatch previews.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Consider whether local handoff guidance should separate external-agent executor contracts, foreground permission surfacing, and bounded workflow previews.

qualifying_updates.visible_date_evidence: Release page shows Sat, Sep 19, 2026 and lists the v0.24.1 changes.
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Qwen Code v0.24.1 added explicit per-subagent tool allowlists, hook invocation progress metadata, configurable external memory providers, browser automation, workflow checkpointing, and named workflow locks.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Subagent coordination and lifecycle-hook leaves should treat tool scope, hook state, and checkpoints as first-class runtime controls rather than prompt-only conventions.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: If ingested, keep broad Qwen release detail upstream and retain only the local least-privilege subagent practice implication.

qualifying_updates.published_or_updated_at: visibly current in 2026-09-24 crawl; paired with 2026-09-19 release and Qwen docs updates
qualifying_updates.visible_date_evidence: The public docs now describe allowlist/blocklist semantics for subagent tools and MCP tool patterns; direct page lacks a visible standalone publication date, so this is tied to the Sep 19 release source rather than counted as a separate release date.
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: The sub-agent documentation says an explicit tools list restricts a subagent to named tools, applies to deferred tool discovery/invocation bridges, and MCP tools must be named explicitly when the subagent has a tools list.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Progressive tool discovery guidance should distinguish discovering tools from granting bridge invocation authority, especially for child agents.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Ingest only if paired with the Sep 19 release evidence; do not treat the undated GitHub page alone as a qualifying dated update.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: The briefing reports terminal-agent movement toward durable local coordination infrastructure, subagent permission scoping as dispatch-time policy, Qwen Code per-subagent tool allowlists, Qwen context-file attribution, and Codex-side changes around child-thread elicitation and structured temporary threads.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: The local practice implication is that agent coordination should be auditable, durable, permission-scoped, and attributable by context source rather than hidden inside prompts or in-memory handoffs.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Route broad product specifics upstream; local page should capture the dispatch-time permission and durable coordination pattern.

qualifying_updates.visible_date_evidence: Article header shows News September 21, 2026 and cites Qwen Code v0.24.2 shipped September 20, 2026.
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Qwen Code v0.24.2 exposed extension ownership in /context detail and added path-conditional instruction rules so file-specific guidance can load only when relevant, with the article quoting Qwen guidance that extension context files are concatenated into every active session request.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Rules and knowledge layers should preserve provenance and cost attribution, and prefer conditional loading for narrow guidance over always-loaded instruction files.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Useful local implication for context-governance pages: attribute context cost by provider/extension and move narrow rules behind path conditions.

qualifying_updates.visible_date_evidence: arXiv page shows Date: Thu Sep 17 10:56:47 2026.
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: The paper introduces state-conditioned minimal sufficient evidence recovery for coding agents and SERBench, arguing retrieval should recover the evidence set a current decision lacks rather than rerank passages by standalone similarity.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Code retrieval evidence guidance should emphasize sufficiency of the set of sources for the current agent decision, not only relevance ranking for individual chunks.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: If ingested, make the local page about retrieval sufficiency practice and evaluation gates, not a broad benchmark encyclopedia entry.

qualifying_updates.visible_date_evidence: Search result exposed Current release v2026.09.21_1 and docs build v2026.09.21_1; opened page describes repo-ready workflow conventions.
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: The AGILab docs describe a repository-ready path for Codex, Claude, Aider, and OpenCode, and frame readiness as committed wrappers/configuration/conventions for each agent path rather than ad hoc setup.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Agent environment readiness and terminal-agent workflow pages can use this as practice evidence for repository-owned entry paths that normalize multiple agent tools while preserving tool differences.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Local implication is repo-readiness as configuration and workflow convention, not product comparison.

qualifying_updates.visible_date_evidence: Opened page shows May 4, 2026 and Updated September 23, 2026.
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: The updated comparison frames Codex CLI, Claude Code, and Gemini CLI as similar user-facing terminal agents with materially different runtimes, sandbox posture, API stacks, model defaults, and context windows.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Terminal-agent workflow and environment-readiness guidance should evaluate runtime/sandbox/API posture explicitly when choosing between compose/build or handoff patterns.

federation_routing.rule: Broad product, model, protocol, and company background remains upstream-owned; this artifact preserves only local-practice implications for selected leaves.

Verify secondary-source product claims against vendor or repository sources during any later ingest.
